meaningMnemonic: You're sitting on your stool again !!? Hints Imagine your super comfy, state-of-the-art stool. You take it everywhere with you, and you're always sitting on it. Again, and again, and again . You love that stool.
readingMnemonic: Your friends are starting to worry about you, because you're always sitting on that stool. "What is the matter ( また ) with you?" they scream! You might want to imagine that all your friends have Jamaican or British accents to make this one fit a bit better! Hints Imagine your friends getting more and more annoyed with your constant stool-sitting habits! They really don't get it. What is the matter with you?! Why can't you just stand like everyone else? Don't you know sitting is the "new smoking"!?

meaningMnemonic: We must stop the moon . That, at least, we can come to an agreement on. Hints There are a group of people pointing at pictures of the moon coming closer to earth. They are the world's leaders, and although they don't get along normally, this new attack from the moon has united them in agreement: we must stop the moon.
readingMnemonic: "We have agreement ," the world's leaders all say. "We will work together to stop the moon, and we have agreement on who we will follow, Emperor こう いち . Hints The world has united against the moon, and they have made Emperor こういち their temporary leader.

meaningMnemonic: If you want to have a tsunami at your wedding , you need to make sure you have it at the bay . Anywhere more inland, and the tsunami won't reach it in time. Hints Picture the tsunami coming towards your beautiful wedding as you stand by the bay. It's not safe, but it's memorable!
readingMnemonic: How did you get a tsunami to show up in the bay in the first place? By throwing a bunch of ura nium ( うら ) in there, of course! Its highly unstable nature can make any body of water, especially a calm bay, turn violent. Hints Imagine throwing buckets of uranium into the bay. It only burns your hands a little. And now they glow green, just like the bay does!

meaningMnemonic: If a tsunami hits a dollar the water will instantly start to boil ! Hints Imagine standing in front of an incoming tsunami. Suddenly in the distance you see someone throwing dollar bills into it and it starts to boil. Ahh!
readingMnemonic: The boil ing water crashes onto the land and you realize your foot is in it! No, not one foot, both your foots ( ふつ )! It hurts so much that you can't even remember the word for two foots. Hints Feel your poor little foots burn in the boiling water. You really want to know who that jerk was that threw dollars into the tsunami to make it boil!

meaningMnemonic: You see horns on a lantern that can hold ten thousand drops of water sitting on the ground . You get closer and realize it's not a lantern, it's actually a bottle . The horns are like a weird handle, but it's definitely a bottle filled with water. Hints Picture this horned bottle sitting on the ground. You don't know who left it here or why, but it's here and the weirdest looking bottle you've ever seen.
readingMnemonic: Even though you're not the one who left this bottle here, you decide to do the right thing and throw it in the trash bin ( びん ). It's not right to leave a bottle just sitting on the ground, you know. Hints Imagine picking up this weird bottle with your bare hands and putting it in a trash bin. You did your good deed for today! Yay!

meaningMnemonic: The call radical and the call kanji are the same. This kanji can also mean eat , because why would you call someone if not to ask them to eat with you?! Hints Call your mom or dad and ask them to go out to eat with you right now.
readingMnemonic: You are call ed to come eat by the Shou gun ( しょう ). He's been really impressed with you lately and he wants to chat over drinks, he says on the phone. Hints Imagine getting a call from the Shougun himself. He's come to your house before, but he's never asked you to eat with him. This is huge!

meaningMnemonic: You try to put your toe inside a shellfish , but it just won't open. That's because this shellfish has sworn an oath of chastity . Hints "No, I won't open up until I meet the toe I will marry," it says to you.
readingMnemonic: " Chastity is really important to me," the shellfish says. "But, maybe if you give me a ta ter ( てい ) tot, I'll change my mind." Hints You give the shellfish a tater tot, and it breaks its vow of chastity, opening up for your toe. You look the other way, but you can hear the sounds of passion below.

meaningMnemonic: There is a special type of meditation where you put a lid on your mouth and touch your forehead down to your legs . If you can do this pose, everything in life will become completely clear . Everything will clear out of your head too. You should try it. Hints Imagine this pose, imagine everything becoming clear. Clear your mind. Clear your head.
readingMnemonic: Your mind is as clear as a sparkling clear pond. On this pond you see yourself in a row ( りょう ) boat. A single row boat on the clear pond that is now your mind. Hints Picture the row boat on the clear pond in your mind. Watch the clear water flow over the row boat's oars.

meaningMnemonic: What outfit do you wear when cutting down tree s with a jackhammer ? A collar . Yup, just a collar… plus some shirt cuffs and slacks, of course. You know, the classic Chippendales look. Hints This collar is what you always wear when you do your "hot lumberjack" act. If you were seriously trying to cut down trees, you wouldn't be using a jackhammer, after all.
readingMnemonic: Your collar has " Eri c" ( えり ) emblazoned on it in cursive letters, because this is the stage name you use when you do your lumberjack act. Eric's not your real name, of course — you just think it sounds hunky and looks good on a collar. Hints Imagine standing there in your collar, jackhammering trees as all your swooning fans scream "Eric! Eriiiic! We love you!" from the audience.

meaningMnemonic: So my building has a big splinter , right in the corner . So what? Hints Imagine a huge splinter coming out of the corner of the building. It's in a really dangerous spot, but the owner doesn't seem so worried about it.
readingMnemonic: That corner is dangerous, but what are you going to do, sue me ( すみ )? Hints Actually, please don't sue me. I'll fix the splinter coming out of the corner of my building.

meaningMnemonic: The buddy building is in the next county . If it was in your county then it wouldn't be a buddy, it would be a neighbor. You're aware of this building, but they aren't that close, so they're just a buddy. Hints Imagine looking at a map of your county and the surrounding ones. All of the buildings in the counties next to yours are buddy buildings!
readingMnemonic: Your county is everything you can reach when shooting a gun ( ぐん ). If the bullet can't reach a building you know, it's a buddy building in another county. Hints Imagine taking out a gun and shooting in a random direction. When you find where the bullet landed, you know that's the county line. Though if it gets stuck in a building or a person it doesn't count. You'll have to try again.

meaningMnemonic: There's a fire next to which you left some syrup , and it has all dried up ! Put any liquid substance near fire and it will dry up actually, but syrup especially. It goes from being sticky and gooey and yummy to a pile of hard, dry sugar. Not so yummy. Hints Imagine pouring some syrup next to a fire and watching it dry up. Watch as the sides slowly bubble and harden and lose what makes syrup so good in the first place.
readingMnemonic: If you dry up syrup like this, you're removing its sou l ( そう ). Have you ever seen dry syrup before? No soul in that. In fact, you probably have no soul if you can dry out syrup like this without feeling bad about it. Hints Go back to imagining a fire drying up some syrup and watch as a tiny little syrup soul cries and is released into the air. Oh no!

meaningMnemonic: If you use a sickle to kill a shrimp you'll need a really good explanation for yourself. What did that shrimp do to you? Why use a sickle? Well? What's your explanation? Hints Try to come with an explanation for picking up a sickle and cutting the head off a shrimp with it.
readingMnemonic: In your explanation you blame everything on Shaq ( しゃく ). He told you to do it! It's all Shaq's fault, you explain. Hints Picture Shaq popping into your head as you struggle to come up with an explanation for me. Picture Shaq's face. This is payback for Shaq Fu, you think, as you finalize the rest of the explanation in your mind.

meaningMnemonic: When the moon faces the right direction , the fat in the bodies of people and animals all gets drawn to the surface and we all look weirdly greasy for a little while. You probably knew that the moon exerts a pull on water, but I bet you didn't know it exerted a pull on fat too! Hints Picture the moon turning to face a different direction. Feel all the fat in your body start to get extracted up through your pores, creating this slick, greasy sheen all over your skin. Let's hope this phase of the lunar cycle ends quickly.
readingMnemonic: As long as you're covered in fat , you might as well go bow ling ( ぼう ). Imagine how smoothly that bowling ball's going to roll after you slather it with some of this fat! Hints Feel how slippery the bowling ball gets as you smear it with fat. Now close your eyes and imagine pins toppling in every direction as your fat-slathered ball careens into them!

meaningMnemonic: You ate the moon with a spoon , and then the sun too, but man were they high in fat ! In fact, you wanted to eat them with chopsticks, but they were so greasy with fat that the spoon was your only option. Hints Imagine staring down regretfully at your fat-covered spoon after eating both the moon and the sun. Not only did you eat two really important celestial bodies, but their high fat content made them way less healthy than you expected.
readingMnemonic: Unbeknownst to you, the moon and sun contained as much fat as an entire adult shee p ( し )! Why didn't you check the nutrition facts first??? Hints If you had known you were going to get a whole sheep's worth of fat, you would have just eaten a big platter of mutton chops instead of dooming the entire solar system by eating the moon and sun.

meaningMnemonic: The leader of Korea is destined for greatness . Hints I mean, they're the leader of Korea already, right? So they have to have a decent chunk of greatness in them already to get that far.
readingMnemonic: The greatness radiates off of the leader of Korea, so much so that you can hardly look. Just when you're about to close your eyes to shield them from the greatness, a great ea gle ( い ) soars over them, letting out a cry. Hints Picture the greatness of the scene before you: the leader of Korea, a great eagle overhead, it's so great!!

meaningMnemonic: You put flowers on your car and your scooter . The flowers you put on them are lotus flowers. Hints Imagine placing lotuses on top of your scooter and car. They are the right kind of flowers for these vehicles.
readingMnemonic: You're putting a lotus on both your scooter and car because they are ren tals ( れん ). Hints You always put a lotus on top of your rental cars and scooters. It just makes those boring, ugly rental cars and scooters so much prettier!

meaningMnemonic: A person with horns has you on the ground and lets loose two poops over your heart . " Mercy ! Mercy!" You cry, but the horned dude doesn't stop until there are two gross poops sitting on your heart. "M-mercy..." is the only thing you can think to say. Hints Imagine yourself saying "mercy" over an over as this horned guy has you on the ground and keeps pooping over your heart.
readingMnemonic: As you shout " Mercy !" one more time, suddenly Je sus ( じ ) appears out of no where and punches the horned guy into the stratosphere. Jesus snaps his fingers and the poop is gone and you're off the ground. Your heart is safe. Hints Imagine yourself saying mercy and seeing Jesus appearing just in time to save the day. The word "mercy" must be his bat signal. Jesus signal? Sure.

meaningMnemonic: The dirt on the forehead of a pig makes a small mound . Picture it, if you will. A pig is rooting through the dirt. It lifts its head and there is a mound of dirt right on its forehead. Hints Imagine that you're the pig. How big can you make your forehead dirt mound?
readingMnemonic: The pig's forehead dirt mound keeps getting bigger until it's the size of two cars ( つか )! Pigs are big, but you didn't think one could balance a mound the size of two cars on its forehead and not fall over. Hints Picture a pig with a mound of dirt the size of two cars leisurely stomping around on a farm.

meaningMnemonic: You have a plow and a (water) well . These are the two things you need in order to plow . Hints You'd think you'd only need a plow, but you also need water if you're going to plow a field, otherwise what's the point?
readingMnemonic: Plow ing all the fields are こう いち s. Not Emperor こういち . These are the こういち clones the government made, and now they're being put to use. Hints Thousands and thousands of こういち s, set free unto the world to do all our plow ing work.

meaningMnemonic: Everyone knows that when a woman plays football she becomes a princess . Thats how princesses are made. Hints Picture the awesome princess, kicking butt and taking names, out on the football field.
readingMnemonic: Remember the word 姫 ? It means princess too. If you remember the ひめ from 姫 , you'll be able to remember this one too. Hints Make sure you know both princess words and you'll know their readings too.

meaningMnemonic: You run your fingers through your husband 's horns . His horns are what you love to put between your fingers. Hints This is one of the perks of having a horned demonic creature for a husband. You can put his horns between your fingers and get a really nice stretch on your finger joints.
readingMnemonic: Why are your husband's horns what you always love to put between your fingers? Because he's a ho t ser geant ( はさ )! Hints Imagine having a strong, muscular sergeant with horns for a husband — so macho! With a husband like that, you'd be running your fingers through his sexy horns every chance you get. Sir, yes sir!

meaningMnemonic: Your clan is breaking ground and building your new residence . You're all working together to make you a new home! Hints Picture your clan, working together, to build a new residence for you on their land.
readingMnemonic: Your new residence is complete! You step closer and the smell of ta ter ( てい ) tots hits your nose. Someone is making you tater tots in your new residence. Wait, no they aren't. Your residence is MADE of tater tots! Thank you, clan! Hints Imagine living in a tater tot residence. Whenever you're hungry, you just lean over to the wall and munch.

meaningMnemonic: What would your mouth do if you got caught in a prison for legs ? It'd probably get real big — in other words, it would scream . Hints Picture a prison for legs. It's like a trap that your legs can never escape, basically. And it's pretty painful, so imagine your mouth opening big and wide and letting out a scream.
readingMnemonic: You scream and scream and scream until a door bursts open. It's Genghis Khan ( かん ) and he looks mad. Apparently your screaming is bothering him and now he's gonna give you a real reason to scream. Hints Imagine Genghis Khan doing something to make you scream. What is it? What could Genghis Khan do that's worse than what's already happening to you?

meaningMnemonic: Flowers that grow in a rice paddy only live to be seedling s. Once they sprout, they're plucked away to make room for more rice. Poor little seedlings. Hints Picture the seedlings growing among the rice plants. Once they bloom they'll be picked, so let's hope they stay small as long as they can.
readingMnemonic: The seedling s try their best to blend in by referring to themselves as myou ( みょう ), you know, me and you combined. That's myou. Hints Listen to the little seedlings say myou over and over. Too bad the farmers can tell they aren't rice plants.

meaningMnemonic: A turkey sitting on a stool is something every ship has in its crow's nest. That's why the universal ship counter is a turkey on a stool. Not a crow. Hints Picture yourself counting ships by pointing your finger from one turkey propped up on a stool to the next. You'll be the best ship counter in the world at this rate!
readingMnemonic: Once you become the best ship counter in the world everyone will think you are super sexy ( せき )! Nothing is sexier than being able to count, and counting ships is the sexiest thing you can count. Hints Imagine yourself, a sexy ship counter. Sexily counting ships. You go guy/girl/non binary person! So sexy!

meaningMnemonic: If you look in a tiger 's stomach you'll find a bunch of skin . It's really gross but what else did you think you'd find? Everyone knows tigers can't digest the skin of the things they eat. Hints Imagine yourself opening a tigers mouth and looking all the way down into its stomach and seeing a bunch of skin. Why would you imagine that? Eww.
readingMnemonic: The only person who would try to take skin from a tiger's stomach is a foo l ( ふ ). You'll probably get your head bitten off looking for skin that way. Hints Imagine a fool trying to pull skin out of a tiger's stomach. You can imagine them getting their skin added to the pile too if you want.

meaningMnemonic: A car that's lack ing is really soft . Cars need to be hard so that things like bugs and other cars won't hurt the people inside when you hit them. But if your car is lacking the hardness it needs, you'll have a really soft, useless car. Hints Picture a soft car lacking what it needs to drive down the road. It's so soft it just flops down and won't move.
readingMnemonic: This car is probably so soft because it's made entirely of naan ( なん ). Naan may be delicious, but it makes a really crappy car. No wonder it was so soft (and yummy). Hints Picture trying to drive this soft naan car. It probably just sinks into the ground and then gets eaten by wild animals (and me).

meaningMnemonic: If you mix a bunch of building s together, you have yourself a suburb . Hints Isn't that all a suburb is? Just a mix of a variety of buildings in one area?
readingMnemonic: " Suburb s are what we need!" says Emperor こう いち . Hints "That suburb life will encourage more people to study kanji," Emperor こういち continues.

meaningMnemonic: Take the street all the way to that geoduck , way up there. When you reach it, you will have made it to the summit . You humbly present the road to the geoduck and bow before it. Hints There is a giant geoduck at the summit of the mountain, and the street will lead you right there. Imagine the grueling climb up the mountain to the summit. Feel it in your legs, and keep looking at that tall, tall geoduck. Now imagine kneeling those same aching legs humbly to the street below the geoduck.
readingMnemonic: You are at the top, the summit of everything! You humbly survey your surroundings from the top of the geoduck, only to see someone on the street, running toward you. It is Mrs. Chou ( ちょう ), and she looks angry. Hints Anytime you use the street, you're in Mrs. Chou's territory. After detecting you were using her street to reach the geoduck, she started coming after you. Remember, wherever there's a street (radical), Mrs. Chou is not far behind.

meaningMnemonic: A tsunami is coming, so you ask two Wolverine s to help you take your turkey out for a wash . Despite the obvious dangers, a giant wave is the only thing that'll wash a giant turkey, so you have no choice. Hints Imagine how big and heavy this turkey must be. It's so huge so you need the strength of two Wolverines and the magnitude of a whole tsunami to move it around and wash it.
readingMnemonic: To make sure your turkey won't get carried away by the tsunami while you wash it, you pin it down with a giant tack ( たく ). If you're washing a giant turkey inside a giant wave, only a giant tack will guarantee it doesn't get washed away. Hints If you want to wash your turkey, make sure to have your special tack ready. The tsunami will recede pretty fast, so you need to tack your turkey to the ground if you don't want the sea to take it.

meaningMnemonic: If you put two mustache s on either side of a tsunami it won't know which way to go and spin back and forth until it becomes a whirlpool . Mustaches are pretty gross, so I don't blame the tsunami for avoiding them. Hints Picture the tsunami spinning in a circle, trying not to hit the mustaches until it spins itself into a giant whirlpool.
readingMnemonic: The whirlpool is huge, and it starts pulling things into itself. Oh no, is that my ca r ( か )? Hey, wait! Whirlpool give my car back! Hints Picture my car getting sucked into the whirlpool. Picture me crying as my car disappears into it forever.

meaningMnemonic: If you have an ear for the public 's heart , you must be very wise . You can understand everything the people want, and you know how to give it to them because you listen to their hearts so well. Hints Close your eyes and open your ears. Feel all of the wise things fill you.
readingMnemonic: All of these wise things are stored in your sou l ( そう ), not your brain. That's where all of these kinds of intuitive feelings live. Hints Picture your wise soul, living inside your body. Somehow it just seems to know what the public really wants. It's like your soul is connected to their souls, granting you this wisdom.

meaningMnemonic: When a tree grows old , it will wither . Hints Old trees' roots and leaves grow inefficient, and they can't get enough nutrients. It's only natural for them to wither up a little bit.
readingMnemonic: This wither ed tree's best friend is a human 子 ( こ ). Imagine the child hugging the tree. Hints It gave the 子 its shade, its sap, and eventually its body to build a house. What an awful child, and what a generic giving tree.

meaningMnemonic: An agreement is determine d by means of affirmation . If both parties are affirming each other's positions, then it's safe to say they probably agree on things. 肯定 is a relatively formal word used for affirming something as correct or valid. It can describe actively agreeing with an opinion or stance, but it's more often used to describe a clear, positive response to a question or claim. It also commonly appears in introspective contexts, like 自己肯定感 (a feeling of self-acceptance), when talking about recognizing yourself or your own life in a positive way.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means call , so the verb version is to call , as in calling someone over. 召す is an honorific verb, so it's used to talk about the actions of social higher-ups. 召す suggests the image of a superior who summons someone or something to themselves, hence the main meaning to call. But it can also be a polite way to say to take , like when they take a meal or a drink, and to wear when talking about their clothes.
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: If a noble decides to call you over, don’t look them in the 目 ( め ). That's super rude! To show respect when you're called, turn away your 目 .
